_meta.rationale: Separate the legislative purpose (protection) from the regulated activity (processing) into two distinct Systems connected by a LEGISLATOR ↔ GOVERNED_SUBJECT Relationship. GDPR-as-System defines what protection requires; DataController-as-System defines how processing achieves it.

systems.name: EU-GDPR
systems._analysis: GDPR as a System in the SaaS SIE instance has its OWN purpose (protection) and its OWN identity-level commitments about HOW it achieves that purpose (through lawful, fair, transparent, proportionate means). These are meta-governance Directives — they govern the governance framework itself. As an internalized representation of the EU legislative framework, this System DOES act: it ingests Regulation state objects (from external legislative sources), compiles them into NormativeDeliverable state objects (structured DPR for governed subjects), and delivers those via the state plane to tenant SIE instances. The EU-GDPR System is the SaaS SIE's normative transformer — it bridges external legislation and tenant governance.

purposes.name: protection-of-natural-persons
purposes._source: Art. 1(2) — protection des personnes physiques à l'égard du traitement des données à caractère personnel

purposes.name: free-movement-of-personal-data
purposes._source: Art. 1(3) — libre circulation des données à caractère personnel au sein de l'Union

directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST ENSURE lawfulness OF protection-of-natural-persons
directives._meaning: The protective framework must operate through lawful means — protection cannot be achieved by violating other legal principles.

directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST ENSURE fairness OF protection-of-natural-persons
directives._meaning: Protection must be fair — not discriminatory, not deceptive, respecting reasonable expectations.

directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST ENSURE transparency OF protection-of-natural-persons
directives._meaning: Protection must be transparent — data subjects must know how they are protected and can exercise their rights.

directives._source: Art. 5(1)(b)(c)(e) — limitation des finalités, minimisation, conservation
directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST ENSURE proportionality OF protection-of-natural-persons
directives._meaning: Protection must be proportionate — constraints on processing should not exceed what is necessary for the protective purpose.

directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST ENSURE accountability OF protection-of-natural-persons
directives._meaning: Protection must be accountable — the framework must produce demonstrable, auditable compliance.

directives._source: Art. 12-22 — droits de la personne concernée
directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST ENSURE rights-enforceability OF protection-of-natural-persons
directives._meaning: Protection must include enforceable individual rights — data subjects are not passive beneficiaries but active rights-holders.

directives._source: Art. 1(3) — la libre circulation ne peut être ni restreinte ni interdite
directives._reads: EU-GDPR MUST PRESERVE non-restriction OF free-movement-of-personal-data
directives._meaning: Protection must not restrict free movement of data within the EU — the two purposes must coexist.

policies.name: processing-requires-lawful-basis
policies._note: GDPR-level Policy: declares WHAT must hold for any governed subject. The DataController System's Policies will translate this into operational predicates.

stateObjectArchetypes.name: Regulation
stateObjectArchetypes._source: External legislative source (EU Official Journal, CNIL, national transpositions)
stateObjectArchetypes._note: Inbound SOA: represents a legislative text as observed from external sources. Instances are created when the SaaS SIE ingests a regulation. The articles array contains structured article content (number, title, paragraphs, cross-references). This is the RAW input — not yet compiled into GSM DPR.

stateObjectArchetypes.name: NormativeDeliverable
stateObjectArchetypes._source: Compiled by EU-GDPR System from Regulation content
stateObjectArchetypes._note: Outbound SOA: structured GSM DPR compiled from Regulation articles, ready for delivery to tenant SIE instances via the state plane. Each NormativeDeliverable targets a specific governed-subject archetype (e.g., DataController, DataProcessor). Tenant SIE instances observe these and adopt/derive their own DPR.

stateObjectArchetypes.name: NormativeCompilationReport
stateObjectArchetypes._note: Audit trail SOA: records what was compiled, what was skipped, what ambiguities were detected. Enables governance traceability from raw legislation to delivered DPR.

functions.name: ingest-regulation
functions._note: Acquire regulation texts from external legislative sources and create Regulation state object instances.

functions.name: compile-normative-requirements
functions._note: Transform Regulation content (articles, recitals) into structured GSM DPR (Directives, Policies, Operationalizations) packaged as NormativeDeliverable instances.

functions.name: validate-normative-coherence
functions._note: Check compiled NormativeDeliverable for internal coherence: Directive conflicts, Policy coverage gaps, unmapped articles, purposeQualifier consistency.

functions.name: deliver-normative-package
functions._note: Publish validated NormativeDeliverable to the state plane for consumption by tenant SIE instances.

functions.name: monitor-legislative-updates
functions._note: Detect amendments, new versions, or supersession of Regulation state objects and trigger recompilation.

eventArchetypes.name: RegulationIngested
eventArchetypes._source: Triggered when a new Regulation SOA instance is created
eventArchetypes._note: Carries regulationId, title, authority, version. Triggers compilation.

eventArchetypes.name: RegulationUpdated
eventArchetypes._source: Triggered when an existing Regulation is amended or versioned
eventArchetypes._note: Carries regulationId, previousVersion, newVersion, amendmentSummary. Triggers recompilation.

eventArchetypes.name: NormativeCompilationCompleted
eventArchetypes._note: Carries normativeDeliverableId, regulationId, principlesCount, policiesCount, coherenceScore.

eventArchetypes.name: NormativeCoherenceViolation
eventArchetypes._source: Emitted when coherence validation detects issues
eventArchetypes._note: Carries normativeDeliverableId, findings (Directive conflicts, coverage gaps, unmapped articles).

eventArchetypes.name: NormativeDeliverablePublished
eventArchetypes._source: Emitted when a validated deliverable is published to the state plane

eventArchetypes.name: LegislativeUpdateDetected
eventArchetypes._note: Carries regulationId, updateType (amendment, supersession, repeal), sourceUri.

rules.name: compile-regulation-to-normative-deliverable
rules.body:
evt = on("RegulationIngested")
regulation = sys.acquire("Regulation", {"id": evt["regulationId"]})
deliverable = sys.create("NormativeDeliverable", {
    "regulationId": evt["regulationId"],
    "version": regulation["version"],
    "compiledAt": now(),
    "targetSystemArchetype": "DataController",
    "principles": [],
    "policies": [],
    "operationalizations": [],
    "validationStatus": "pending",
    "coherenceFindings": [],
    "coverageGaps": []
})
report = sys.create("NormativeCompilationReport", {
    "regulationId": evt["regulationId"],
    "normativeDeliverableId": deliverable["id"],
    "compiledAt": now(),
    "articlesProcessed": 0,
    "principlesExtracted": 0,
    "policiesExtracted": 0,
    "unmappedArticles": [],
    "ambiguities": [],
    "coherenceScore": 0.0
})
sys.emit("NormativeCompilationCompleted", {
    "normativeDeliverableId": deliverable["id"],
    "regulationId": evt["regulationId"],
    "principlesCount": 0,
    "policiesCount": 0,
    "coherenceScore": 0.0
})
rules._note: Skeletal Rule: the compilation logic body is intentionally simplified. In practice, the Definition Sourcer's legal-regulatory adapter performs the deep article→DPR extraction. This Rule captures the governance lineage (why the compilation happens) and the structural markers (which SOAs are created/acquired).

rules.name: validate-normative-deliverable-coherence
rules._note: Validates compiled DPR for coherence before publishing. If violations found, emits NormativeCoherenceViolation (human review needed). If clean, marks as validated and publishes to state plane.

rules.name: handle-legislative-update
rules.body:
evt = on("LegislativeUpdateDetected")
regulation = sys.acquire("Regulation", {"id": evt["regulationId"]})
if evt["updateType"] == "repeal":
    result = sys.modify("Regulation", {"id": evt["regulationId"]}, {"status": "repealed"})
    sys.emit("RegulationUpdated", {"regulationId": evt["regulationId"], "previousVersion": regulation["version"], "newVersion": None, "amendmentSummary": "repealed"})
else:
    result = sys.modify("Regulation", {"id": evt["regulationId"]}, {"version": evt["newVersion"], "amendments": evt["amendments"]})
    sys.emit("RegulationUpdated", {"regulationId": evt["regulationId"], "previousVersion": regulation["version"], "newVersion": evt["newVersion"], "amendmentSummary": evt["amendments"]})
    sys.emit("RegulationIngested", {"regulationId": evt["regulationId"]})
rules._note: Handles legislative amendments and supersession. On amendment: updates Regulation SOA, triggers recompilation via RegulationIngested. On repeal: marks regulation as repealed (downstream NormativeDeliverables become stale).

operationalizations._note: The compilation rule operationalizes lawfulness: it ensures that normative deliverables correctly encode lawful-basis requirements for governed subjects.
Same Rule: compilation extracts rights requirements from regulation articles.
Accountability is operationalized through validation: the coherence check produces auditable evidence of compilation quality.
Legislative updates can change lawful-basis requirements — the monitoring rule ensures normative deliverables stay current.

realizations._note: The compilation function realizes protection by translating legislative intent into enforceable DPR.
Validation ensures the compiled DPR is coherent — incoherent normative deliverables would undermine protection.
Delivery serves both purposes (protection AND free movement) — normative packages enable compliant data processing across the EU.
Monitoring serves both purposes: legislative changes can affect protection requirements AND free movement conditions.
Ingestion feeds both purposes: updated regulation content flows into compilation for both protection and free movement.

systems._note: EU-GDPR is an OPERATIONAL System in the SaaS SIE instance: it ingests Regulation state objects from external legislative sources, compiles them into NormativeDeliverable state objects (structured GSM DPR), validates coherence, and publishes to the state plane for consumption by tenant SIE instances. This is the normative transformation pipeline — the bridge between external legislation and tenant governance. The EU-GDPR System's DPR governs HOW that transformation happens (lawfully, transparently, proportionately, accountably). The DataController System in tenant SIE instances observes NormativeDeliverable instances and adopts/derives its own DPR.

systems.name: DataController
systems._analysis: The data controller as a System has its OWN concrete business purposes — Art. 5(1)(b) requires that data be 'collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes'. Each purpose is a reason WHY the controller processes personal data. Art. 5 quality dimensions are prefixed 'personal-data-processing-' to specify WHAT is being qualified: the processing of personal data (not generic qualities). They are cross-cutting: they qualify ALL purposes equally. GSM models this via wildcard purposeScope (null) on Directives.

purposes.name: analytics-and-improvement
purposes._note: Usage metrics, A/B testing, product improvement.

purposes.name: legal-compliance
purposes._note: Tax reporting, audit trails, regulatory filings.

directives._note: purposeScope null = wildcard: applies to ALL purposes. The 'personal-data-processing-' prefix specifies WHAT is being qualified — the processing of personal data, not generic lawfulness.

policies.name: privacy-information-completeness
policies.predicate: PrivacyNotice.includesControllerIdentity == true && PrivacyNotice.includesPurposes == true && PrivacyNotice.includesLegalBasis == true && PrivacyNotice.includesRetentionPeriod == true && PrivacyNotice.includesDataSubjectRights == true

rules.name: handle-access-request
rules.body:
evt = on("DataSubjectAccessRequest")
subject = sys.acquire("DataSubject", {"id": evt["dataSubjectId"]})
if subject == None:
    sys.emit("RequestDenied", {"requestId": evt["requestId"], "reason": "identity-not-verified"})
else:
    records = sys.acquire("PersonalData", {"dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"]})
    sys.emit("AccessResponseProvided", {
        "requestId": evt["requestId"],
        "dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"],
        "purposes": records["purposes"],
        "categories": records["categories"],
        "recipients": records["recipients"],
        "retentionPeriod": records["retentionPeriod"],
        "source": records["source"],
        "responseDate": now()
    })

rules.name: handle-erasure-request
handle-rectification-request
rules.body:
evt = on("DataSubjectRectificationRequest")
subject = sys.acquire("DataSubject", {"id": evt["dataSubjectId"]})
if subject == None:
    sys.emit("RequestDenied", {"requestId": evt["requestId"], "reason": "identity-not-verified"})
else:
    result = sys.modify("PersonalData", {"dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"]}, {"correctedFields": evt["corrections"]})
    sys.emit("RectificationCompleted", {"requestId": evt["requestId"], "dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"], "correctedFields": evt["corrections"], "rectifiedAt": now()})
    sys.emit("RecipientNotificationRequired", {"dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"], "action": "rectification", "correctedFields": evt["corrections"]})

rules.name: handle-portability-request
validate-processing-lawfulness
rules.body:
evt = on("DataProcessingActivityCreated")
activity = sys.acquire("DataProcessingActivity", {"id": evt["activityId"]})
lawful_bases = ["consent", "contract", "legal-obligation", "vital-interests", "public-interest", "legitimate-interests"]
if activity["lawfulBasis"] not in lawful_bases:
    sys.emit("LawfulnessViolation", {"activityId": evt["activityId"], "declaredBasis": activity["lawfulBasis"], "validBases": lawful_bases, "severity": "ERROR"})
else:
    sys.emit("LawfulnessValidated", {"activityId": evt["activityId"], "lawfulBasis": activity["lawfulBasis"]})

rules.name: enforce-consent-withdrawal
rules.body:
evt = on("ConsentWithdrawn")
activities = sys.acquire("DataProcessingActivity", {"dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"], "lawfulBasis": "consent"})
for activity_id in activities["ids"]:
    alt_basis = sys.acquire("DataProcessingActivity", {"id": activity_id})
    if not alt_basis["hasAlternativeLawfulBasis"]:
        result = sys.modify("DataProcessingActivity", {"id": activity_id}, {"status": "ceased", "ceaseReason": "consent-withdrawn", "ceasedAt": now()})
        sys.emit("ProcessingCeasedDueToConsentWithdrawal", {"activityId": activity_id, "dataSubjectId": evt["dataSubjectId"]})

systems._structural_traceability_note: Function↔Purpose traceability is now structural (no Realization primitive): Function ← Mechanism/Controller → Rule → Operationalization → Policy → Directive → Purpose. Each Mechanism references exactly one Function; Controllers are auto-derived from Rule bodies. Cross-cutting Functions (serving ALL purposes) are identified by wildcard purposeScope (null) on Directives whose Operationalization chains reference the Function's implementing Rule.

relationships._source: Art. 4(7) — the data controller is subject to GDPR
relationships._note: The DataController defines this Relationship from its perspective: 'I am a GOVERNED_SUBJECT of EU-GDPR (LEGISLATOR)'. This is the governance channel through which GDPR's protection Directives translate into the controller's processing Directives.

strengths: Purpose names are semantically precise: 'protection' for GDPR, concrete business purposes for controller.
Directive sentences read naturally in BOTH systems — and wildcard purposeScope eliminates 14×N combinatorial explosion.
EU-GDPR System is operational in SaaS SIE: it ingests, compiles, validates, and delivers normative packages — the regulation-to-DPR transformation pipeline.
Clean LEGISLATOR ↔ GOVERNED_SUBJECT Relationship models the governance channel.
Maps exactly to the SaaS multi-tenant model: GDPR System exists per SIE instance, tenant Systems consume via Relationship.
DataController purposes are REAL business purposes (Art. 5(1)(b) 'specified, explicit and legitimate purposes') — not the processing activity itself.

Wildcard Directives capture the cross-cutting nature of Art. 5 correctly: 'personal-data-processing-lawfulness' qualifies ALL purposes, not each one individually. The prefix specifies the governed domain (personal data processing), not generic qualities.
weaknesses: Two Systems to model one regulation's effect — more complex.
DataController Directives are 'copies' of GDPR constraints, not formally derived — GSM has no 'inherited DPR' mechanism (intentional: Components don't inherit DPR).
The governance channel (Relationship) is declared but HOW Directives traverse it is undefined in GSM — it's a governance process question, not a model question.
The GDPR System's Policies reference DataController properties (e.g., 'DataController.allProcessingActivitiesHaveLawfulBasis') — cross-system Policy predicates may be a GSM design frontier.
The compilation Rule body is skeletal — real article→DPR extraction requires the Definition Sourcer's legal-regulatory adapter (LLM + structured output), not pure Starlark logic.
Cross-SIE-instance state plane interaction (SaaS → Tenant) is architecturally described but not yet formalized in GSM — how does a tenant SIE 'observe' a NormativeDeliverable from the SaaS SIE?

wildcard_purposeScope.change: Directive.purposeScope cardinality: '1' → '0..1'. When null, applies to ALL Purposes of the owning System.
wildcard_purposeScope.grammar: Current: 'System Modal Verb PurposeQualifier OF Purpose'. Extended: 'System Modal Verb PurposeQualifier' (when purposeScope is null — OF-clause omitted, qualifier applies universally).
wildcard_purposeScope.rationale: Cross-cutting quality commitments (lawfulness, fairness, transparency) are identity-level — they characterize the System itself, not a specific Purpose. Art. 5 GDPR is the canonical example: these principles apply to ALL processing regardless of specific purpose. Without wildcard, 14 qualifiers × N purposes = 14N Directive instances — combinatorial explosion that adds no governance information.
wildcard_purposeScope.systemics_grounding: Beer's identity function (S5) defines what the system IS — unconditionally. Cross-cutting Directives are S5-level commitments: they characterize the system's constitutional identity, not its specific activities. Scoping them to individual Purposes forces identity-level concerns into activity-level granularity.
wildcard_purposeScope.impact_on_gsm_puml: Directive.purposeScope changes from '0..* o--> 1 Purpose' to '0..* o--> 0..1 Purpose'. Validation rule updated: purposeScope MAY be null (wildcard). Coverage gap detection: wildcard Directives cover all Purposes by definition — gaps only arise when a specific Purpose has contradicting specific-scope Directives.
wildcard_purposeScope.conflict_detection: Wildcard Directives conflict with specific-scope Directives on the same purposeQualifier. Resolution: specific-scope wins (more specific). Wildcard × wildcard conflict: same as today (modal precedence).

open_questions: Should GDPR's Policies reference DataController properties? Or should they stay abstract and let the DataController's own Policies be the measurable translation?
Is the Directive 'duplication' (same qualifiers in both Systems) a feature (explicit adoption) or a problem (redundancy)?
Could GSM model 'DPR adoption through Relationship' — a governed subject's Directives being formally derived from a legislator's Directives via the governance channel?

Should wildcard Directives expand to specific-scope Directives at save time (materialized), or remain wildcard and expand at evaluation time (virtual)? Trade-off: materialized enables per-purpose conflict detection; virtual is simpler but hides purpose-specific governance gaps.

How does cross-SIE-instance state plane interaction work? Does the SaaS SIE expose NormativeDeliverable SOAs through an API? Through event bus? Through a shared state store? This is an architecture question, not a GSM question.

Should NormativeDeliverable carry full GSM DPR JSON (self-contained) or references to SaaS-side definitions (federated)? Trade-off: self-contained enables tenant autonomy; federated enables live updates but creates coupling.

The EU-GDPR System exists in the SaaS SIE instance — should it also exist (as a reference/shadow) in tenant SIE instances for Relationship anchoring? Or does the tenant only see the NormativeDeliverable SOAs without knowing the producing System?

cross_sie_architecture.description: The EU-GDPR System operates in the SaaS SIE instance as a normative transformer — bridging external legislation and tenant governance through the state plane.
flow: 1. External source (EU Official Journal, CNIL) → publishes regulation text
2. SaaS SIE: monitor-legislative-updates detects new/updated regulation
3. SaaS SIE: ingest-regulation creates Regulation SOA instance
5. SaaS SIE: validate-normative-deliverable-coherence checks compiled DPR
6. SaaS SIE: deliver-normative-package publishes NormativeDeliverable to state plane
7. Tenant SIE: observes NormativeDeliverable via state plane
8. Tenant SIE: DataController System adopts/derives its own DPR from normative content
9. Tenant SIE: Supervision plane evaluates DataController compliance against adopted DPR
cross_sie_architecture.key_insight: Regulation texts are state objects PRODUCED by the legislative system (EU Parliament → CNIL → ...). The EU-GDPR System in SaaS SIE internalizes and transforms them. The state plane is the bridge between SIE instances — NormativeDeliverable SOAs are the medium of cross-instance governance.
